Article Title: Elon Musk fires another salvo over Starlink delay, targets Ambani again
Article Text:
Musk argued that Starlink could improve access to the internet in underserved parts of the country

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Friday fired another salvo over the delay in the commercial rollout of Starlink in India, taking swipe at billionaire Mukesh Ambani once again.In a post on X, Musk addressed the Reliance Industries chairman as “Prime Minister Ambani”, alleging that he was the “real boss of India” and questioning why Starlink was yet to receive the necessary clearances to begin commercial operations.“Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?” Musk wrote.He argued that Starlink could improve access to the internet in underserved parts of the country, particularly for children seeking educational opportunities and small businesses looking to reach international markets.“There are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no Internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and for small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better. Thank you” he added.Musk's latest remarks come a day after he accused unnamed Indian business groups of obstructing Starlink's entry to protect their market positions.He had alleged that the company was being blocked by “certain oligarchs” seeking to maintain a “monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people”.The Indian government has rejected the allegations, maintaining that the delay stems from pending regulatory and security requirements rather than preferential treatment for domestic telecom companies.At the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi, Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said India would not permit a monopoly in any sector and that three satellite communication operators had received licences.These include Reliance Jio Satcom, Bharti Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Starlink. Amazon's Project Kuiper has also expressed interest in entering the market and will undergo the standard evaluation process.Scindia said the government was finalising the satellite spectrum pricing framework, while security assessments by the Ministry of Home Affairs and other agencies were under way. Commercial operations can begin once the companies meet the prescribed requirements.The government has also said security clearances remain pending for all three licensed operators, rejecting the suggestion that Starlink alone is facing regulatory hurdles.
Article Summary: Musk addressed the Reliance Industries chairman as ‘Prime Minister Ambani’ He questioned why Starlink was yet to receive the necessary clearances to begin commercial operations. He argued that Starlink could improve access to the internet in underserved parts of the country.

Article Title: UPI vs credit cards: What should you choose for payments after MDR?
Article Text:
An often-overlooked aspect of credit card payments is that their value is not limited to rewards.

The author is CEO of Paisabazaar

UPI and cards serve different purposes in the consumer wallet

What determines value of a payment?

Value-back as rewards or cashback can change the economics

Transaction size alone does not determine the better choice

Does Transaction Size Decide the Payment Method?

Credit cards can offer value beyond the immediate transaction

The consumer's spending pattern should drive the choice

Before you tap, scan, or swipe: Check these 6 things

MDR may change the equation, but not necessarily in the same way for everyone

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

When it comes to choosing between UPI and credit cards, consumers should look at the overall value that they can derive from each payment method rather than the immediate cost of the transaction. While UPI provides convenience and simplicity, credit cards offer cashback, rewards and additional perks. With MDR on higher-value UPI transactions now being discussed, understanding the complete economics of a transaction becomes even more important.The overall value of a transaction depends on several factors including the payment mode, transaction value, the applicable MDR (if any), and the value-back attached to the payment method. This becomes particularly relevant as UPI increasingly intersects with the credit card ecosystem through RuPay credit cards.When a consumer makes a UPI payment from a bank account, the money is deducted directly from the account. While this offers simplicity and convenience, such payments generally do not come with any meaningful rewards, apart from occasional merchant-specific offers.A credit card changes this equation. The consumer can make the purchase today and get an interest-free period of 40-50 days, depending on the card's billing cycle and payment terms.Moreover, when it is a RuPay Credit Card that supports UPI payments, this flexibility is combined with the convenience of UPI.Credit cards are increasingly being designed around specific spending behaviours. Depending on the card, consumers can earn cashback or reward points on categories ranging from everyday purchases to high-ticket spends like travel bookings and electronics.Consider a Rs. 50,000 transaction on a card offering 5% cashback on the spend. The consumer could potentially receive Rs 2,500 back, subject to the card's terms, redemption value and applicable caps. Now if the consumer chooses to pay the same amount through UPI and the merchant passes on the entire MDR cost of 0.4% to the consumer, they will end up paying an additional Rs 200, making the product costlier for them, with no additional benefits.In fact, in most scenarios, credit cards can offer greater value to consumers through rewards, cashback and other benefits, without any additional payment processing charges being levied on them. However, this holds true only if consumers pay their credit card bills in full and on time, avoiding interest or finance charges. Once interest starts accruing on outstanding balances, it can outweigh the value earned through rewards or cashback, potentially nullifying the benefits of using a credit card.This is why comparing payment methods purely on the basis of transaction charges like MDR could be misleading. Rewards, offers and other value-back systems should also be taken into account. At the same time, a card may carry an annual or joining fee, impose reward caps, exclude certain categories, or offer a lower reward rate on certain transactions – which should also be considered.A common assumption is that UPI is best suited to small purchases while cards make more sense for larger transactions. However, in practice, the answer is more nuanced.Even a small Rs 500 transaction on a credit card could be more valuable than the same transaction through bank-account UPI if the card offers meaningful cashback or rewards on that particular spend. Conversely, a Rs 50,000 transaction may not necessarily justify the use of a credit card if the transaction falls outside the card's reward categories or has already exhausted the applicable monthly reward cap.Consumers should, therefore, look at the frequency of spending and the cumulative rewards generated over time. Small individual transactions can add up to significant value when they form a large portion of monthly expenditure. At the same time, card-specific discounts, cashback, merchant offers and reward points may add further value. Hence, the effective benefit can vary considerably across cards and merchants, irrespective of transaction values.An often-overlooked aspect of credit card payments is that their value is not limited to rewards. For consumers who manage their credit responsibly, the interest-free period can provide useful cash-flow flexibility. Some transactions may also be eligible for EMI conversion, allowing a large purchase to be spread across several months. Credit cards also come with issuer-specific offers, milestone benefits, travel privileges and more.But these benefits only have value when they are actually relevant to the consumer. Paying an annual fee for benefits that are rarely used does not necessarily make economic sense.Ultimately, there is no single payment method that will offer the best value for every consumer or every transaction. The important shift is to stop looking at payment methods only through the lens of convenience or transaction value and instead consider the net economics of the payment and choose the payment instrument that delivers the most meaningful value for one's individual spending pattern.The discussion around MDR on higher-value UPI transactions adds another dimension to this comparison. MDR represents a cost associated with accepting a digital payment, and the relative economics for merchants can vary across payment instruments and transaction types.The impact on consumers, however, will depend on how the ecosystem responds. If merchants absorb the additional cost, there may be little or no visible impact on the consumer. If the cost is reflected in pricing or an additional payment-related charge, consumers may have to pay it as part of the product’s cost.Whether and to what extent merchants pass such costs on to consumers is yet to be seen.
Article Summary: Credit cards are increasingly being designed around specific spending behaviours. Consumers should look at the overall value that they can derive from each payment method rather than the immediate cost of the transaction. Even a small Rs 500 transaction on a credit card could be more valuable than the same transaction through bank-account UPI.

Article Title: Patrón co-founder John Paul DeJoria turned a 96-acre Texas ranch into a home for more than 120 exotic animals; when it sold for $6.93 million, the buyer inherited the herd and a 2,700-square-foot unde
Article Text:
The ranch, known as “Patrón de Paz,” was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin.

A ranch that came with more than a house

The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms.

The underground shelter

The animals were part of the deal

Why DeJoria sold the ranch

DeJoria co-founded Patrón Spirits Company in 1989.

A 96-acre Texas ranch once owned by Patrón Tequila co-founder John Paul DeJoria came with an unusual combination of luxury, wildlife and an underground shelter. More than 120 exotic African animals lived on the property, while the estate also had a 7,540-square-foot main house, two barns, a stocked pond, a pecan orchard and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The ranch, known as “Patrón de Paz,” was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin, and stretched along 2,600 feet of Fitzhugh Creek. According to the Houston Chronicle, the property was listed for $7.495 million in 2016 after initially being put on the market for $7.99 million. It eventually sold for $6.93 million. As reported by ABC13 Houston, television director Jonathan Nowzaradan is the buyer of the ranch.The property was not simply a large Texas home. Its listing described it as an exotic-animal ranch, and the buyer was set to inherit more than 120 exotic African animals. According to the Houston Chronicle, the animals were part of the property when it was listed. The ranch included two barns, each with attached guest quarters, along with a stocked pond and a pecan orchard. As reported by The San Antonio Express-News, the animals included more than 120 exotic species and that the property was being sold with the animals and its furnishings.The estate itself covered 96 acres and overlooked Fitzhugh Creek, which feeds from Barton Creek. The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms. It featured wood-beamed ceilings, hardwood floors, partial stone walls and a large gourmet kitchen with a commercial-grade stove. Outside, there was a pool and spa, an outdoor kitchen and a wide porch overlooking the surrounding Hill Country.One of the property's more unusual features was underground. As reported by The San Antonio Express-News, the ranch included a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The Austin Business Journal also described the property as having a “2,700-square underground shelter.” So, when the ranch changed hands, the buyer was getting far more than a luxury residence. The property came with its land, buildings, underground shelter and a large collection of exotic animals.The exotic animals were among the details that made the ranch unusual in the first place. As reported by The Houston Chronicle, the new owner would inherit more than 120 exotic African animals. The ranch was a 96-acre property with a spa pool, limestone walls and the animals. The animals included species such as gazelles, wildebeest and antelopes.DeJoria, best known for co-founding John Paul Mitchell Systems and Patrón Spirits Company, had owned Patrón de Paz since 2008, as reported by the San Antonio Express-News. Realtor Dave Murray said DeJoria's primary residence was near Lake Austin and that he had decided to sell the Dripping Springs ranch. Murray also said DeJoria owned several other homes around the world and was selling four estates at the time. DeJoria co-founded John Paul Mitchell Systems with hairdresser Paul Mitchell in 1980 and later co-founded Patrón Spirits Company in 1989. The ranch's sale meant that its next owner did not simply acquire a large piece of Texas Hill Country property. The $6.93 million deal also brought with it a ready-made exotic-animal ranch, two barns, a creekside estate, a stocked pond and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter.
Article Summary: The ranch, known as ‘Patrón de Paz,’ was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin. The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms. The ranch included two barns, a stocked pond, a pecan orchard and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The new owner would inherit more than 120 exotic African animals.

Article Title: Dear Prime Minister Ambani, accept my apologies: Elon Musk
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In the ongoing war of words over the ongoing satellite communication services in India by Starlink, Elon Musk has launched his shrillest ever attack on Mukesh Ambani In a late night post on X, the Starlink boss said: "Dear Prime Minister Ambani, please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?""There are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no Internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and for small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better. Also, Starlink has proven to be essential for saving lives during natural disasters throughout the world, when all other communications systems have failed, so you would also be helping save men, women and children throughout India," Musk's latest post said.The fresh expression of anger over the alleged delay in approving satellite communication services in India - something all the three licence holders, with the other two being Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio are facing - began Wednesday and he has been cranking the heat each passing day since then.On day one, he accused "certain oligarchs" of "blocking" Starlink's entry to India without naming anyone but saying "you can guess who they are." The second day, he followed up by naming Ambani and asking, "is Ambani the real boss of India." And on day three, he said, "Dear Prime Minister Ambani."Govt has denied the charges. Telecom minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said at the India Mobile Congress: "There is a lot of conversation about a particular party (Starlink).But there are three parties (Mittal, Jio and Musk) that have got licenses... We are very clear on our stand. As and when govt decides the charge system on revenue basis that spectrum will be assigned to them and as and when they individually fulfil security conditions, they can start operations." Billionaire Jeff Bezos-led Amazon's Project Kuiper is eyeing a licence to do so."India does not allow monopoly in any sector, " the minister said."Govt is technology agnostic. Our job is to provide a bouquet of services. In a free market, it is upto the customers to choose which service they want to opt for and then which service provider with that service bouquet. Govt's responsibility is to lay out a predictable regulatory architecture so that companies can make their capex decisions," Scindia said.The minister further said that the Union govt is "close to taking the final decision with respect to (spectrum for satcom) pricing regime. TRAI has made some recommendations and the DoT is engaging with it on that".
Article Summary: Starlink boss Elon Musk has launched his shrillest ever attack on Mukesh Ambani. In a late night post on X, the Starlink boss said: "Dear Prime Minister Ambani, please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India"

Article Title: I-T finds stamp duty, tax evasion in Karnataka land deals
Article Text:
Under lens: Tax authorities have alerted the registration department in Karnataka

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tax authorities in Bengaluru have come across a new tool for evading taxes and stamp duty, a development that may have implications across states. Initial estimates suggest land deals of over Rs 300 crore have seen under-reporting.The income tax department's directorate of intelligence and criminal investigation in the southern city has found several instances of incomplete disclosure of the entire sale consideration in the registered sale deeds.The remaining amount is paid by executing unregistered full and final settlement deeds with the payment routed through banking channels.There are several instances of the method being used by local builders to purchase land parcels and then develop them into residential units and plots."Since the additional payment made is not part of the sale deed, the buyer pays no stamp duty and registration fee to the state govt, resulting in huge revenue loss," said a person familiar with the probe.The tax authorities have alerted the registration department in Karnataka. Stamp duty evasion in the state can result in hefty penalties.Besides, the buyers did not deduct TDS despite purchasing 'urban agricultural land' as a result of which the additional amount paid through full and final settlement deed remained outside the radar of the tax department.Some of the sellers, who have claimed exemption from the sale of agricultural land have not filed their returns, as a result of which tax was not paid."The department also identified a number of registered transactions involving exchange of property involving undervaluation of properties sold, on which there is short payment of stamp duty and registration fee and payment of additional consideration outside the book," said a person in the know.The findings call for a revision in the guidance value of the land which is adjacent to urban areas and align the prices to market rates."The circle rate is significantly lower than the market rate, which is resulting in these kind of transactions," an official said.
Article Summary: Tax authorities in Bengaluru have come across a new tool for evading taxes and stamp duty. Initial estimates suggest land deals of over Rs 300 crore have seen under-reporting. There are several instances of the method being used by local builders to purchase land parcels and then develop them.

Article Title: SC junks challenge to TN speaker's call to accept ADMK plea to condone 21 'rebels'
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Friday refused to entertain an AIADMK party worker's petition challenging the Tamil Nadu speaker's decision to accept AIADMK's plea to withdraw disqualification petitions against 21 of its legislators who had defied party orders and voted for the confidence motion moved by the governing TVK.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said when the party, to which the MLAs belonged, has condoned the lapse and withdrawn its petitions seeking their disqualification, a person who is not even an MLA cannot challenge the speaker's decision.The petitioner said that by their very conduct, the 25 MLAs, of whom four have resigned, have indulged in anti-party activity and are liable for disqualification under the anti-defection law.The Supreme Court bench said in a multi-party democracy like India, political dynamics in a coalition govt must be left to the political parties and decisions in this regard by the speaker, unless palpably unconstitutional, cannot be interfered with by the courts.The Madras high court had earlier dismissed the appellant's writ petition against the speaker's order dropping disqualification proceedings against the 21 MLAs.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court Friday refused to entertain an AIADMK party worker's petition challenging the Tamil Nadu speaker's decision. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said when the party, to which the MLAs belonged, has condoned the lapse and withdrawn its petitions seeking their disqualification, a person who is not even an MLA cannot challenge the speaker's Decision.

Article Title: SC: Nothing wrong in deleting dead or those who've shifted
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday said there is nothing wrong in deletion of names of the dead, and those who have either shifted out from the ward or duplicate names during Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls but said that on the date of notification of elections, the voter list which is final - either the post-SIR list or the one on Jan 1, 2026, would be used for local body polls in Andhra Pradesh.A bench of chief justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to entertain YSR Congress Party's appeal against Andhra Pradesh high court's decision rejecting its plea for deferment of local body elections till finalisation of SIR of electoral rolls.The bench said SIR is a necessity as those who have passed away or shifted cannot be allowed to vote in the wards. The duplicate voters' names also are required to be struck down, and these are the anomalies that are taken care of through SIR, it said.On the plea that HC has directed finalisation of post-SIR voter list by Oct 16, the bench said as per the legislations governing the panchayat, municipalities and municipal corporations, the elections would be held based on the final voter list available on the date when the EC notifies the elections.When the SEC said that the election dates have not been notified and that it would be bound to take the final voter list available on the election notification date, the bench agreed and said if for some reason the post-SIR final electoral rolls are not published prior to the election notification, then the EC would consider holding polls based on the voter list as finalised on Jan 1, 2026.
Article Summary: Supreme Court said there is nothing wrong in deletion of names of the dead, and those who have either shifted out from the ward or duplicate names during Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. A bench of chief justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to entertain YSR Congress Party's appeal.

Article Title: Chemists, wholesalers may need government nod to advertise prescription drugs
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Chemists, wholesalers and drug distributors may soon have to seek Centre's approval before advertising certain prescription medicines, with health ministry proposing to extend existing curbs on advertisements of Schedule H, H1 and X drugs to those involved in their sale and distribution.The proposal assumes significance as regulators have raised concerns over promotion of potent prescription medicines, including antibiotics, hormonal preparations, psychotropic drugs, anti-cancer medicines, narcotic drugs and life-saving injectables.The ministry has now proposed inserting a new sub-rule under Rule 65 of Drugs Rules, 1945, stating no advertisement of drugs specified in Schedule H, H1 or X shall be made without previous sanction of central govt. The provision would apply to those holding licences to sell, stock, exhibit, offer for sale or distribute such drugs.Importantly, the proposal does not mean that advertisements of these medicines are currently freely permitted. Drugs and Cosmetics Rules already require prior govt sanction for advertisements of Schedule H, H1 and X drugs.
Article Summary: The proposal assumes significance as regulators have raised concerns over promotion of potent prescription medicines. The provision would apply to those holding licences to sell, stock, exhibit, offer for sale or distribute such drugs. Drugs and Cosmetics Rules already require prior govt sanction for advertisements of Schedule H, H1 and X drugs.

Article Title: NEET cancellation exposed NTA gaps: Parliamentary panel
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Seeking a sweeping overhaul of NTA after the NEET-UG 2026 question paper was leaked despite biometric checks, jammers and AI-monitored CCTVs, a Parliamentary panel has recommended making the medical entrance exam computer-based, creation of secure question banks and investment of NTA's accumulated surplus in govt-run test centres.The parliamentary standing committee on education, chaired by Congress MP Mukul Wasnik, said the cancellation despite strengthened safeguards demonstrated the need for "greater procedural and institutional reforms". Its 35 observations and recommendations include an independent mechanism to audit examination security and report directly to the education ministry. After the 2024 controversies, the panel questioned whether security upgrades alone can safeguard examinations.Acknowledging that NTA conducts examinations involving around 1.2 crore candidates annually, the panel welcomed reforms introduced since 2024. However, it flagged structural weaknesses, arguing that rebuilding public trust required more than new surveillance measures.The scale of disputes has been substantial. NTA's 2024-25 report recorded 474 court cases, including 356 concerning NEET-UG 2024. The panel said restoring confidence required a "two-way communication", rather than engagement largely restricted to portals and notifications.
Article Summary: The NEET-UG 2026 question paper was leaked despite biometric checks, jammers and AI-monitored CCTVs. Parliamentary panel has recommended making the medical entrance exam computer-based, creation of secure question banks and investment of NTA's surplus in govt-run test centres.

Article Title: Not anti-business but firm on ending crony capitalism: Rahul Gandhi
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A day after SpaceX chief Elon Musk's accusation against the Modi govt, Rahul Gandhi said Congress is committed to breaking the chain of crony capitalism, and that India needs a level-playing field with every business having a fair chance to compete.In an X post, Rahul said, "Congress and I are committed to ... building an economy driven by innovation and hard work - not political patronage." The opposition neta waded into the controversy, as Musk hit out at the Ambani group, saying it was behind the lack of govt action on Starlink's request for licence.In their X exchange, Rahul told Musk, "Wait till you discover the other guy." It was an unnamed reference to Adani. The US tycoon thanked Rahul for his reply and said, "This is indeed troubling." In a video montage posted on social media as a follow-up, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha said, "I am not anti-business; I am anti-monopoly."
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi said Congress is committed to breaking the chain of crony capitalism. In an X post, Rahul said, "Congress and I are committed to... building an economy driven by innovation and hard work - not political patronage" The opposition neta waded into the controversy, as Musk hit out at the Ambani group.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Val Kilmer turned a 5,328-acre New Mexico ranch into a retreat with rental cabins and a B&B; he asked $33 million in 2009, then sold most of the property two years later when the asking price fell to
Article Text: Val Kilmer’s sprawling Pecos River ranch in New Mexico went from a private Hollywood escape to a high-end hospitality retreat before eventually changing hands in 2011. Contemporary reports from CBS News and the Associated Press, along with real-estate publications including The Land Report, documented the property’s years-long journey from a $33 million listing to its eventual sale after a steep reduction in the asking price.Located about 22 miles northeast of Santa Fe in San Miguel County, the ranch stretched across 5,328 acres and followed a particularly scenic section of the Pecos River. The property was known for its river frontage, natural springs, wildlife and extensive trails through New Mexico’s high-desert landscape. A later account from Realtor.com described the ranch as largely wild, with canyons and pine forests surrounding its residential buildings.Kilmer had acquired the land in the 1990s and spent years developing it into a secluded base away from Hollywood. Earlier coverage by the Los Angeles Times described the ranch as containing guest cottages, staff quarters, stables, barns and corrals, while Kilmer kept horses and other animals on the property. He had also previously attempted to sell portions of the ranch, including an approximately 1,800-acre section listed for $18 million in 2006.By 2009, Kilmer had changed strategy and put the entire ranch on the market. The Land Report reported an asking price of $33 million, with the property offering several homes and outbuildings as well as more than five miles of Pecos River frontage. The listing represented a significant escalation from his earlier attempts to sell smaller portions of the ranch.The property’s price subsequently dropped sharply. By late 2010, reports said the ranch had been reduced to $18.5 million, down from $23 million earlier that year. The AP also reported that the ranch included more than 10 natural springs, hiking and riding trails, guest quarters and a large main residence.The ranch was not simply a private residence. Kilmer had sought permission to operate guesthouses as overnight accommodations, eventually receiving approval from San Miguel County after controversy surrounding remarks he had previously made about the region. The Los Angeles Times reported that the proposed lodging involved three guesthouses, while contemporary coverage described the property as operating as a bed-and-breakfast with rental cabins.Its history also extended well beyond Kilmer. The land formed part of the larger Forked Lightning Ranch associated with oilman Buddy Fogelson and actress Greer Garson. According to the National Park Service, Fogelson purchased the original 5,500-acre ranch in 1941, and he and Garson later used it as a residence and gathering place for prominent figures from Hollywood and beyond. After Fogelson’s death, the property was divided among his heirs, with portions eventually passing to Kilmer and actress Jane Fonda.After several years on the market, most of Kilmer’s Pecos River property was finally sold in 2011. CBS News reported that the buyer was Texas oil and gas executive Benjamin A. Strickling III and his wife, Roxann. The deed transfer was recorded on September 30, 2011, according to contemporary property reports. The $18.5 million figure represented a dramatic reduction from Kilmer’s original $33 million asking price, amounting to roughly 44% below the initial listing.The sale marked the end of Kilmer’s long chapter on the Pecos River, where he had built not just a home but a sprawling private retreat around the landscape. The property later remained associated with conservation and outdoor recreation, while the larger historic Forked Lightning Ranch continues to be preserved in part through Pecos National Historical Park.What do you think about this? Tell us your views in the comments section below.
Article Summary: Val Kilmer's 5,328-acre Pecos River ranch in New Mexico went from a $33 million listing to its eventual sale after a steep reduction in the asking price. Kilmer had acquired the land in the 1990s and spent years developing it into a secluded base away from Hollywood. After several years on the market, most of the property was finally sold in 2011.

LUCKNOW: Indian Railways has ordered the cancellation of all Mail and Express trains departing from their originating stations after 2pm on Friday and scheduled to reach New Delhi or Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4am and 2pm on Saturday, Oct 10, citing anticipated severe road traffic congestion around the two stations.The directive, issued by the Railway Board’s coaching directorate on Oct 9, has led to the cancellation of several important services connecting Lucknow, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Varanasi and other parts of Uttar Pradesh with the national capital. Several return services from Delhi have also been cancelled.Northern Railway confirmed the cancellation of Lucknow Mail (12229) and Lucknow-New Delhi AC Superfast Express (12429), both scheduled to depart Lucknow on Friday.North Central Railway announced the cancellation of Prayagraj Express (12417), Prayagraj-New Delhi Humsafar Express (12275), Kanpur Central-New Delhi Shram Shakti Express (12451) and Manikpur-Hazrat Nizamuddin UP Sampark Kranti Express (12447), all scheduled to depart on Friday.The Kanpur Central-New Delhi Shatabdi Express (12033) and Agra Cantt-New Delhi Intercity Express (14211), scheduled for Saturday, have also been cancelled.Northeastern Railway confirmed the cancellation of Shiv Ganga Express (12559) and Banaras-New Delhi Superfast Express (12581), both originating from Banaras on Friday. Their corresponding return services, New Delhi-Banaras Express (12560) and New Delhi-Banaras Express (12582), scheduled for Saturday, have also been cancelled.In addition, the railway announced the cancellation of Kasganj-New Delhi Express (15303) and both services of the Lucknow-New Delhi Tejas Express, train numbers 82501 and 82502, scheduled to operate on Saturday. The cancellation of Tejas, a premium train connecting the state capital with New Delhi, is expected to affect passengers travelling to and from Lucknow over the weekend.The Moradabad division also cancelled the Dehradun-New Delhi Jan Shatabdi Express (12056), scheduled for Saturday.Besides long-distance trains, several passenger services have been affected. North Central Railway cancelled Aligarh-Delhi MEMU (64151), Dankaur-Delhi EMU (64107) and Khurja-Ghaziabad EMU (64113) for Friday.For Saturday, the cancelled services include Aligarh-Delhi EMU (64101 and 64103), Khurja-Shakur Basti EMU (64111), Hathras Qila-Delhi MEMU (64581), Tundla-Delhi MEMU (64583), Aligarh-New Delhi EMU (64105) and Dankaur-Shakur Basti EMU (64109).Moradabad division separately announced the cancellation of additional passenger services, including Moradabad-Delhi (54307), Bareilly-Delhi (54075), Delhi-Bareilly (54076) and service number 64567 between Bulandshahr and Tilak Bridge, on their respective notified dates.Meanwhile, North Central Railway announced the operation of a special unreserved train between Mathura Junction and Virangana Lakshmibai Jhansi Junction on Saturday to accommodate additional passengers during the proposed non-interlocking work at Mathura Junction and Bateshwar Yard.Train number 01901 will depart Mathura Junction at 4pm and reach Jhansi at 9pm, with stoppages at Agra Cantt, Dholpur, Morena, Gwalior, Dabra and Datia. The special train will operate for one trip only.The widespread cancellations come ahead of planned demonstrations in central Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Oct 10.While the Railway Board’s initial directive anticipated severe road congestion without specifying its cause, subsequent cancellation notices issued by the Moradabad railway division explicitly referred to the proposed protests in central Delhi and the accompanying traffic advisory.
Article Summary: All Mail and Express trains departing from their originating stations after 2pm on Friday and scheduled to reach New Delhi or Hazrat Nizamuddin on Saturday will be canceled. The directive, issued by the Railway Board’s coaching directorate on Oct 9, has led to the cancellation of several important services. Several return services from Delhi have also been cancelled.

Article Title: Retail dal prices surge by Rs 20-30 a kg across Mumbai Metropolitan Region
Article Text:
Pulse prices at the wholesale market rose by an average of Rs 15 from the previous month because of tight local supplies.





NAVI MUMBAI: Prices of major pulses have risen by Rs 10-20 per kg in Vashi APMC wholesale market in recent weeks amid supply shortages, deficient monsoon rainfall, drought conditions, higher logistics costs and festive demand. Retail prices have increased by Rs 20-30 per kg.Pulse prices at the wholesale market rose by an average of Rs 15 from the previous month because of tight local supplies.Grain, Rice and Oilseeds Merchants’ Association (GROMA) president Bhimji Bhanushali said lower food grain arrivals followed drought conditions across Maharashtra. Wholesale price increases were being reflected in retail markets, where restrictions were limited, he said. Rohan Sawant, a consumer, said the recent hike in prices has disturbed the kitchen budget badly. Wholesale chana prices climbed from Rs 72 to Rs 82 per kg over the past month, while retail prices increased from Rs 110 to Rs 130. Tur prices rose from Rs 90 to Rs 105 per kg at APMC, while retail tur dal averaged about Rs 150 per kg, up from Rs 120 in Mumbai Metropolitan Region. Wholesale moong dal prices increased from Rs 95 to Rs 105 per kg, while retail prices averaged Rs 140.A wholesaler said prices could continue rising because of production losses in growing regions across Maharashtra and elsewhere in the country. Bhanushali said major pulse-producing states received below-average rainfall during the June-Sept monsoon, prompting drought declarations in parts of Karnataka and Maharashtra. Millers and stockists had also increased inventories before the festive season, while annual increases in minimum support prices affected selling prices. APMC grain market director Nilesh Veera said premium Kolam rice prices had risen from Rs 50 to Rs 60 per kg over the past fortnight, while basmati rice prices were also affected. Basmati rice prices rose by an average of Rs 5 per kg, while wheat and millet prices remained unchanged. Veera said govt was considering reducing import duty on pulses to stabilise the local market, but its impact was yet to be seen.
Article Summary: Pulse prices at the wholesale market rose by an average of Rs 15 from the previous month because of tight local supplies. Wholesale chana prices climbed from Rs 72 to Rs 82 per kg over the past month. Tur prices rose from Rs 90 to Rs 105 per kg at APMC, while retail tur dal prices, up from Rs 120 in Mumbai Metropolitan Region.

Article Title: 'PERM distinct from H-1B visa': MEA on US move to suspend certain firms from green card programme
Article Text:

Which companies have been suspended?

What is PERM, and how is it different from H-1B?

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday said the US government's decision to suspend several technology companies from the employment-based green card programme would not, by itself, affect existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents.The ministry said the suspension of applications under the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme could, however, affect the permanent residency process for eligible employees of the companies concerned.“We are aware of the US Department of Labour’s decision concerning the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme for certain companies. It should be noted that PERM is distinct from the H-1B visa programme,” the MEA said in a statement.“The suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents, though there could be some impact on the permanent-residency/Green Card process of eligible employees of the affected companies,” it added.The ministry also emphasised the economic benefits of skilled talent moving between India and the US, saying the latest measures did not advance the shared ambitions of the two countries.“It should also be clear that talent mobility adds value to both economies. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US,” the MEA said.“This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact. The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries,” it added.The US department of labour has suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini from the PERM programme. The department said it would not accept new applications from the affected companies or process their pending applications amid multiple active federal investigations.US labour secretary Keith Sonderling said the companies had collectively sought millions of foreign workers and received hundreds of thousands of approvals under employment-based immigration programmes.“Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost 3 million foreign workers. They received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications. That's hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers,” Sonderling said.The administration has alleged that companies misused employment-based immigration programmes to replace American workers with foreign employees. These are allegations made by US officials; the announcement cited ongoing investigations.PERM is a labour-certification process that allows an eligible US employer to sponsor a foreign worker for employment-based permanent residency, commonly known as a green card. Before certifying an application, the US department of labour must establish that there are not enough qualified and available American workers for the job and that employing the foreign worker would not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed US workers.The H-1B programme, by contrast, allows US employers to hire skilled foreign workers temporarily for specialised occupations. The PERM suspension does not automatically cancel existing H-1B visas, but it could disrupt a route to permanent residency for employees whose employers are sponsoring them through the programme.The move comes amid a wider crackdown by the Trump administration on skilled foreign labour. A day before the announcement, the US department of homeland security proposed new fees for F-1 international students seeking to participate in Optional Practical Training (OPT), describing the measure as an effort to protect American workers and strengthen the integrity of the immigration system.
Article Summary: The US government has suspended several technology companies from the employment-based green card programme. The move comes amid a wider crackdown by the Trump administration on skilled foreign labour. Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini have been suspended.

Article Title: American billionaire Mark Cuban to Americans: You are getting the 'job killer' wrong, it is not AI; it is your rising ...
Article Text:
The cost picture of US health care

What the research says

Why costs are rising

Mark Cuban's own stake

American billionaire and Shark Tank judge Mark Cuban has warned that rising healthcare costs, rather than artificial intelligence could pose a bigger threat to jobs in the United States. The founder of Cost Plus Drugs said increasing employer healthcare expenses may lead to more layoffs and reduced hiring in the years ahead. In a post shared on social media platform X (forlmekry known as Twitter) Cuban wrote, “I hope people realize that for the foreseeable future, the cost of healthcare benefits will get more people fired, or not hired, than AI." The comments come at a time when fears around AI-driven job losses continue to dominate workplace discussions. However, Cuban argued that soaring healthcare expenses are placing a greater burden on employers, forcing businesses to rethink hiring plans and workforce costs.According to a report by Fortune, the United States spends more on health care than any other country, and the total has climbed sharply. The most recent figures from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services show $5.3 trillion in spending in 2024, about 18% of GDP. That is more than double the $2.5 trillion spent in 2000. On a per-person basis, the U.S. spent $14,775 in 2024, nearly double the $7,860 spent in other high-income countries.Some studies find Americans use less care on average.Employers are feeling the squeeze. A Mercer survey of more than 1,800 employers found health care costs have risen every year for the past five years. Mercer estimates that cost per employee could rise 8.2% in 2027, the biggest jump since 2003. Nearly half of large U.S. employers, those with 500 or more employees, expect to change their medical plans next year, Mercer found. Common changes include higher deductibles or copays that raise workers' out-of-pocket costs.Part of Cuban's claim has academic support. A 2024 paper from Yale's Tobin Center for Economic Policy found that a 1% rise in health care prices leads to a roughly 0.4% drop in payroll and employment at employers outside the health sector. "Rather than cutting wages, employers respond to increases in insurance premiums by cutting the number of workers they employ," the paper said. The study measures health care prices' effect on employment. It does not compare that effect with the effect of AI, which is the comparison Cuban made. Fortune did not cite research on that point.Fortune pointed to several causes: higher labor costs, new technology and pricier treatments such as GLP-1 medications. Some experts also cite structural problems in the U.S. health care system, including hospital consolidation and rising administrative costs.Cuban is best known as a former Shark Tank investor and longtime Dallas Mavericks owner. He has become deeply involved in the health care industry since launching Cost Plus Drugs, an online discount pharmacy, in 2022.For the past four years, he has offered consumers a lower-cost route to prescription drugs. He says the company can charge less by bypassing pharmacy benefit managers. According to the nonprofit KFF, the three largest PBMs manage about 80% of prescription claims in the US. Cuban has also drawn attention to the growing health care costs that companies face.
Article Summary: Shark Tank judge Mark Cuban says rising healthcare costs may lead to more layoffs and reduced hiring in the years ahead. The comments come at a time when fears around AI-driven job losses continue to dominate workplace discussions. The United States spends more on health care than any other country, and the total has climbed sharply.

Article Title: Michael Dell, biggest donor to Trump Accounts, defends change in rules; says: Hard for me to believe that's a bad thing, these children are going to somehow be negatively ...
Article Text:
Moving beyond low-cost index funds

Dell noted that private sector participation is picking up speed:

Michael Dell has come out strongly in defense of updated federal regulations governing Trump Accounts, dismissing warnings from skeptics who claim that permitting donors to gift individual corporate shares directly into children’s portfolios poses ethical or financial hazards. Speaking this week in an interview with Yahoo Finance, the Dell Technologies founder and billionaire philanthropist rejected allegations that such donations are part of an effort to manipulate young minds or asset markets.“It’s kind of hard for me to believe that’s a bad thing, right?” the tech titan said, adding, “That these children are going to somehow be negatively influenced because they now have one share of SpaceX , but they didn’t have before, right? The alternative is they didn’t have it, right?”“It seems unlikely that that is some kind of devious plot to somehow influence these 2 million children. If anything, they’re going to be interested in space and capitalism and how capital markets work, compounding and investing, and it will spark an interest in them that hopefully helps them as they become adults,” he added.Trump Accounts, originally authorised under last year's One Big Beautiful Tax bill, are tax-advantaged savings and investment tools structured to help children build nest eggs for retirement, college education or launching a business.Under the inaugural framework, all account contributions were required by law to sit in low-cost index funds to maximise market diversification.However, rule changes enacted last week permit charitable organisations and donors to place individual company equities into children’s accounts. So far, SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell stands as the only major donor to commit corporate equity under the revised guidelines, promising more than 2 million shares of SpaceX stock to assist lower-income youths aged 11 to 17 living in disadvantaged communities.The policy alteration has drawn sharp criticism from financial analysts and ethicists who caution that directing children’s wealth toward single corporate entities ties their future economic baseline to an isolated business rather than broad, resilient market indices. Moreover, it has been alleged that wealthy donors could potentially orchestrate massive equity contributions to children’s funds as a means to capture tax write-offs or support corporate share prices.Michael Dell’s $6.25 billion pledge and the drive for automatic enrollmentDell and his wife, Susan, represent the single largest private donor block for the program. The couple has committed $6.25 billion to deposit $250 directly into the accounts of 25 million American children. As of October 7, more than 10 million children had received their $250 deposits, totaling $2.6 billion deployed, with the remaining balance of the full $6.25 billion pledge expected to clear by Friday (October 9).“I believe there will be a number of additional philanthropists that join us. We have now many employers that are joining in the fund here and either matching the government's contribution or going much larger and contributing to the accounts of the children that work inside their companies or even children in the communities where they operate their businesses.”The private contributions coincide with a major administrative pivot by the U.S. Department of the Treasury. On October 1, the agency transitioned Trump Accounts from a voluntary setup to automatic enrollment, establishing accounts for nearly 70 million American children under the age of 18 who hold a valid Social Security number.
Article Summary: Dell Technologies founder and billionaire philanthropist rejects allegations that such donations are part of an effort to manipulate young minds or asset markets. Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged savings and investment tools structured to help children build nest eggs for retirement, college education or launching a business.

Article Title: Developers sent letters offering $10,000 to every household in a rural town in the US if a data center is built; almost everyone rejected the offer, and everyone has the same concern
Article Text:
Representative AI image

Why residents rejected the $10,000 data centre offer

A developer offered to give every household in a small Pennsylvania town $10,000 if they agreed to a massive data centre project. The money could pay for rent, groceries, fuel or even help someone buy a car. But the offer has failed to win over many residents, who fear the project could damage their homes, disrupt their lives and change their community. NorthPoint Development sent letters to households in Hazle Township, Pennsylvania, offering a total of $45 million to 4,500 households if the township allowed the proposed data centre project to go ahead, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.The plan involves building the first of 15 data centre buildings across 1,300 acres in the Pocono foothills. The proposed project, however, has faced strong local opposition, with residents raising concerns about noise, property values and the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure. For a town where the median household income is about $60,000, the proposed $10,000 payment represents a significant sum. Yet many residents interviewed by the Journal said they were not keen to accept the project, even with the money on offer.For Jeff Fasnacht, a retired teacher who lives near the proposed site, the main concern is what the development could do to his property's value. He believes the payment would not make up for a possible fall in the value of his home. “$10,000 doesn’t match how much it’s going to tank my property value,” Fasnacht told the Journal.Diana Spallone, a special-education teacher who also received the letter, shared similar concerns. She and her husband recently spent money on home improvements, including a new roof. While the proposed payment could help replenish their savings, she worries that the data centre could ultimately hurt the value of their property.“$10,000 would be nice,” Spallone said.Others are concerned about what the project could mean for the wider community. Some residents fear years of construction noise, while others distrust large developers and worry that towns are not being given enough information before major projects are approved.Ed Negra, a retired homeowner helping organise opposition, believes the cash offer could have the opposite effect to what the developer intended.“I think it works the opposite way, because most people have the opinion that, ‘hey, are they trying to bribe us here?’” Negra told the Journal.NorthPoint's chief marketing officer, Brent Miles, said the idea of direct payments emerged after an angry public meeting last year, when residents questioned what they would gain from supporting the project. “I think we’ve got something here that’s on the cutting edge,” Miles told the Journal, “really in direct response to ‘what’s in it for me?’”The company has also proposed another $120 million in payments over 15 years for police services and other community investments. Miles said the company had persuaded some residents who were initially sceptical by answering questions about water use, energy costs and noise.However, the project remains uncertain. Hazle Township rejected it on zoning grounds in November, after which NorthPoint sued the township to overturn the decision.
Article Summary: NorthPoint Development sent letters to households in Hazle Township, Pennsylvania, offering a total of $45 million to 4,500 households. The plan involves building the first of 15 data centre buildings across 1,300 acres in the Pocono foothills. The proposed project has faced strong local opposition, with residents raising concerns about noise, property values and the rapid expansion of AI.
