Article Title: Panvel civic body to pay Rs 22.8 crore and take over 51 schools in Raigad ZP
Article Text:
The Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) general body has approved a proposal to take over 51 schools of Raigad Zilla Parishad (RZP) by paying about Rs 22.8 crore. These school plots and structures are collectively worth Rs 55 crore.

Navi Mumbai:





The Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) general body has approved a proposal to take over 51 schools of Raigad Zilla Parishad (RZP) by paying about Rs 22.8 crore. These school plots and structures are collectively worth Rs 55 crore.The PCMC general body had in Feb 2021 passed a resolution to take over the RZP schools and a plot in Koynavele. A committee headed by the additional chief engineer, RZP, was formed in 2022 for valuation of the school properties. The committee did the valuation of anganwadis, gram panchayat buildings, schools, community halls, health sub-centres, fish market, among others.The amount has been finalised after adjusting about Rs 22 crore towards the stamp duty receivables and Rs 10.42 crore expenditure incurred on the schools. At the time of payment, the exact amount after evaluation may be changed.The PCMC has a provision of Rs 40 cr in its 2026-27 budget to take over RZP schools. The resolutions passed by the RZP with its relevant documents will be validated by the joint director, town planning, Konkan division. The final amount will be decided upon receiving the report from the divisional town planning department. The PCMC general body has given a green signal to take over the schools.The Panvel civic body will handle the education of the children enrolled in these schools, and the teachers and staffers, after completion of the formalities. A long-standing conflict between the two govt agencies has been resolved.
Article Summary: The Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) general body has approved a proposal to take over 51 schools of Raigad Zilla Parishad (RZP) by paying about Rs 22.8 crore. These school plots and structures are collectively worth Rs 55 crore. A committee headed by the additional chief engineer, RZP, was formed in 2022.

Article Title: After Friday’s heatwave in Mumbai, IMD warns it’ll be a hot and humid Saturday
Article Text:
The India Meteorological Department issued a yellow alert for hot and humid conditions at isolated places on Saturday

Mumbai:





The city continued to swelter for the second consecutive day on Friday with the Santacruz weather station — which is considered the benchmark for Mumbai — recording a maximum temperature of 37.8°C, slightly higher than Thursday’s 37.6°C and 4.7°C above normal.The last seven days saw the Santacruz observatory record three of the 10 highest Oct temperatures since 1951 when record keeping started — 37.4°C on Oct 3, 37.6°C on Oct 8 and 37.8°C on Oct 9.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) retained its yellow alert for a heatwave in Mumbai and Thane on Friday, and issued a yellow alert for hot and humid conditions at isolated places on Saturday.IMD attributed the spike in temperatures to an anticyclone over Mumbai and its neighbouring areas, which has stalled the sea breeze that normally brings relief from daytime heat along the coast.IMD’s Colaba observatory logged a maximum of 37°C, which was 4.4°C above normal and also among the highest Oct recordings since 2014, when it recorded 37°C on Oct 17. The highest during the period was 37.2°C on Oct 30, 2018. Santacruz station’s reading of 37.8°C was the third highest for the month of Oct in 12 years, along with Oct 10, 2018, with the highest being 38.6°C on Oct 17, 2015, followed by 38°C on Oct 29, 2018.Relative humidity recorded by Colaba and Santacruz observatories were 81% and 73%, respectively.IMD scientist Sushma Nair explained: “An anticyclone is a circulation pattern that causes air to sink towards the ground. The system over Mumbai is well organised, and clear, cloudless skies have further contributed to the rise in temperatures.” She said the system was expected to become less organised and shift slightly on Saturday, bringing some relief. Easterly and northerly winds, which are relatively dry, are also influencing weather conditions over the region.Weather experts said prevailing northeasterly and easterly winds over Maharashtra were delaying the development of the sea breeze, allowing temperatures to climb across the Konkan region, where several locations have recorded 38–39°C.Despite the withdrawal of the monsoon from Mumbai on Oct 3, which is earlier than is normal withdrawal date of Oct 8, Sept saw largely dry conditions with limited thunderstorm activity which is generally observed during withdrawal of monsoons also being absent.For Mumbai and other coastal areas, the IMD’s heatwave criteria take into account both the absolute temperature and its departure from normal. A heatwave is declared when the maximum temperature reaches at least 37°C and is 4.5°C or more above normal for two consecutive days.Graphics:MUMBAI’S OCTOBER HEAT:37.8°C — Santacruz, Friday37°C — Colaba, Friday+4.7°C — Santacruz above normal+4.4°C — Colaba above normal38.6°C — Santacruz’s October high since 2014 (Oct 17, 2015)37.2°C — Colaba’s October high since 2014 (Oct 30, 2018)
Article Summary: Santacruz weather station recorded a maximum temperature of 37.8°C, slightly higher than Thursday’s 37.6°C and 4.7°C above normal. India Meteorological Department issued a yellow alert for hot and humid conditions at isolated places on Saturday.

Article Title: BMC may suspend water supply to municipal pools in Mumbai again
Article Text:
BMC headquarters

Mumbai:





Nearly two months after restoring water supply to municipal swimming pools, BMC is considering reviewing its decision as stocks in the seven lakes serving Mumbai remain below last year’s levels and temperatures begin to rise.Water supply to municipal pools was suspended on June 17 and was resumed on Aug 16 after rainfall picked up across the state and lake levels improved. “But there is a need to reassess this decision as harsher summer conditions were emerging, indicating that water demand would increase in coming months. We also need to account for supplies until the next monsoon,” a senior BMC official said.BMC had disconnected water supply to around 128 construction sites in May, including those paying civic water charges, and has not restored it, added the official. A 10% citywide water cut, imposed on May 15, remains in force.BMC data showed that on Oct 8, the seven lakes held 13.3 lakh million litres, or around 94% of their combined capacity, against 14.3 lakh million litres, or 99%, on the same date last year. Stocks in 2024 were 14.3 lakh million litres, or 98.6%. Modak Sagar was at 69% capacity, compared with 99% last year and 95% in 2024. An official said water from Modak Sagar, which receives supplies from Vaitarna system and acts as a balancing lake, was being used before Vaitarna’s gates were opened.Mayor Ritu Tawde said: “The civic administration’s priority is to provide adequate water to citizens. Therefore, whatever steps are needed to ensure that citizens are given first priority will be taken.”
Article Summary: Water supply to municipal pools was suspended on June 17 and was resumed on Aug 16. Stocks in the seven lakes serving Mumbai remain below last year’s levels. A 10% citywide water cut, imposed on May 15, remains in force.

Article Title: Where did last year’s Rs 3,000-crore relief package go, Danve asks govt
Article Text:
State govt has yet to clarify the status of the pending assistance or announce a timeline for disbursing fresh aid to the drought-affected farmers

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Shiv Sena (UBT) MLC Ambadas Danve on Friday slammed BJP-led Mahayuti govt over the alleged non-disbursal of financial aid to drought-hit farmers, questioning the fate of the Rs 3,000-crore relief package announced last year, of which nearly Rs 500 crore in dues allegedly remained unpaid.Raising the issue amid mounting agrarian distress, Danve accused govt of making lofty announcements without ensuring that relief actually reached farmers on the ground. “Govt had announced a Rs 3,000 crore package last year. Where did that package go? Around Rs 500 crore from last year is still pending. This is the question we are raising,” Danve said.The MLC also sought clarity on the assistance planned for farmers affected by the ongoing drought, saying while govt had identified drought-hit talukas, it had yet to spell out the nature or timeline of financial support. “Govt has announced the number of drought-affected talukas. It should now tell farmers what assistance it intends to provide and when,” he said.Danve took a swipe at govt’s handling of the agrarian crisis and said farmers continued to suffer severe financial stress. “Farmers are dying by suicide every day. Such is the grim situation they are facing,” he said.Backing the criticism, All India Kisan Sabha president Rajaj Kshirsagar alleged that farmers reeling from repeated crop losses had been denied timely compensation and support.“Farmers facing successive agricultural setbacks have been seeking timely compensation and financial support to manage mounting losses. But govt is least concerned about the farmers, who are ending their lives unable to bear the stress,” Kshirsagar said.Congress city district president Syed Akram echoed the opposition’s concerns, saying the core issue was the widening gap between govt assurances and the actual delivery of relief. “Danve’s criticism reflects the concerns raised by all opposition parties. We are demanding accountability for pending dues and a clear commitment on fresh relief for farmers,” Akram said.
Article Summary: BJP-led Mahayuti govt slammed over alleged non-disbursal of financial aid to drought-hit farmers. MLC Ambadas Danve questioned fate of Rs 3,000-crore relief package announced last year. Nearly Rs 500 crore in dues allegedly remained unpaid.

Article Title: Upset over unpaid salary, former staffer of cash management firm plots ATM hard disk thefts, held
Article Text:
Investigators said the firm never filed a police complaint in any of the thefts, despite the missing devices containing crucial CCTV footage

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





What allegedly began as a disgruntled employee’s attempt to recover three months’ unpaid wages has exposed an ATM surveillance equipment theft racket, with Parbhani police arresting a former cash management services (CMS) technician and his associates on Thursday on charges of stealing hard disks from at least 27 ATM kiosks across Maharashtra Investigators said the firm never filed a police complaint in any of the thefts, despite the missing devices containing crucial CCTV footage.According to police, Vishal Dhaktode(20) of Mukundwadi in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar had worked as a CCTV technician with the cash management firm responsible for maintaining ATM surveillance systems. “Dhaktode quit his job earlier this year after his employer allegedly withheld three months of salary. Frustrated over repeated failed attempts to recover his dues, he removed hard disks from three public sector bank ATM kiosks and refused to return them till he was paid,” police said.The strategy apparently worked. Police said the firm eventually cleared his pending salary and recovered the stolen hard disks, purportedly choosing a quiet settlement over legal action to avoid reputational damage and potential scrutiny from the bank.But what started as an act of retaliation allegedly snowballed into a larger operation. “During the investigation, we found that the gang had allegedly stolen 27 hard disks. What is particularly concerning is that the firm had not registered an FIR in any of these incidents, despite the thefts involving equipment containing CCTV footage,” Parbhani superintendent of police Pankaj Kumawat said.While the theft of a hard disk does not affect ATM operations or customer transactions, it effectively erases stored surveillance footage, potentially hampering investigations into crimes committed at the kiosks.The wider racket came to light during a probe into the theft of hard disks from three public sector bank’s ATMs in Parbhani city in the early hours of Thursday. The targeted kiosks were located near Bhikulal Petrol Pump, Kanti Chowk and Mahatma Phule Colony on Super Market Road.A joint team of local crime branch (LCB) and Nanapeth police nabbed Sachin Uday Yadav (23) and Prafull Shankar Sonawane (22) of Jalna within hours of receiving information about the thefts. Investigators then traced and Dhaktode in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.LCB inspector Gajendra Sarode said coordinated police action led to rapid breakthroughs in the case. “We acted swiftly after receiving information about the three ATM thefts in Parbhani. Two suspects were detained within two hours, and our team subsequently apprehended the third accused in Sambhajinagar,” he said.Nanapeth police have registered a case under relevant provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita sections 331(4), 305, 62 and 3(5) and seized three 4TB hard disks, a motorcycle, two cellphones, two screwdrivers and a black bag from the accused. The total value of the seized property is estimated at Rs 3.02 lakh.Investigators are now probing the full extent of the alleged network and examining why repeated thefts of sensitive ATM surveillance equipment failed to trigger any formal complaint from the company entrusted with securing them.
Article Summary: Police arrest former cash management services (CMS) technician and his associates on charges of stealing hard disks from at least 27 ATM kiosks across Maharashtra. Investigators said the firm never filed a police complaint in any of the thefts, despite the missing devices containing crucial CCTV footage.

Article Title: ​​GMCH irregularities: Probe panel summons health activists
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: The state inquiry into alleged irregularities at Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar has moved to the next stage, with health activists and former members of the board of visitors summoned to appear before the probe committee on Friday.The four-member panel, headed by Dr Sushil Deshmukh, dean of GMCH, Nanded, has directed Pravin Shinde and Iqbal Singh Gill to appear in person with documents and submissions related to complaints filed through the state’s ‘Aaple Sarkar’ grievance portal.On Oct 3, the panel members visited GMCH, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, to retrieve bills, work orders, and rate comparison charts, among other details concerning the alleged irregularities, corruption, and inflated procurement. However, during that visit, the panel did not officially record the complainants’ testimonies, forcing them to lodge fresh complaints on the ‘Aaple Sarkar’ portal.The inquiry panel has been mandated to investigate the sanctioning of 27 ‘small constructions’ worth around Rs50 crore—allegedly executed without proper authorisation—the purchase of drugs and machinery at inflated rates, and a Rs33 lakh expenditure recorded for a 30-minute in-house event.These matters revolve around Dr Shivaji Sukre, who holds the additional charge as dean of GMCH and is currently under scrutiny.Several insiders from the hospital have called for a rigorous investigation by the panel. “The reputation and image of GMCH have suffered like never before, eroding the faith of underprivileged patients. The inquiry must be fair and speedy, and panel members must not succumb to any pressure or allurements,” a senior doctor from GMCH said on the condition of anonymity.The hearing will be held at the regional office of the Directorate of Medical Education and Research ( DMER ) in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.Dr Syeda Afroz Fatima, dean of GMCH, Jalna, serves as the member secretary of the panel. Its other members include Dr Prakash Gattani, head of the pharmacology department at GMCH, Jalna, and JS Lakhade, administrative officer at DMER, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.
Article Summary: The inquiry panel has been mandated to investigate the sanctioning of 27 ‘small constructions’ worth around Rs50 crore. The purchase of drugs and machinery at inflated rates, and a Rs33 lakh expenditure recorded for a 30-minute in-house event.

Article Title: ​Nanded district administration cuts red tape to ease rabi credit flow to farmers
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Farmers battered by kharif crop losses in Nanded district could find it easier to secure loans to sow their rabi crops. The district administration has removed three key administrative hurdles that were holding up crop credit.The move is aimed at ensuring that farmers who lost their kharif crops are not starved of working capital for the next season.District collector Rahul Kardile has issued three orders to streamline loan disbursal.Banks can no longer insist on No Objection Certificates (NOCs) from farmers occupying Class-2 land. Tehsildars have also been directed to immediately remove old Bhu-Vikas Bank (Land Development Bank) loan burdens still appearing on farmers’ 7/12 land extracts. The administration has further ordered correct Class-2 entries for permanent allottees of ‘gairan’ land.“The objective is to ensure timely availability of working capital for the rabi season and remove unnecessary procedural bottlenecks in crop loan supply. We expect strict compliance from both the revenue and banking machinery with our latest orders,” Kardile said.Farmers’ rights activists welcomed the measures. They now want the “Nanded model” replicated across Maharashtra.“Even if the kharif season is largely destroyed due to a poor monsoon in rain-fed areas, farmers with irrigation facilities can take up rabi crops. Many such farmers have also lost their kharif crops. They need financial support to undertake rabi cultivation,” farmers’ rights activist Jayaji Suryawanshi said.The intervention comes amid widespread farm distress in Marathwada. Delayed monsoon rainfall reduced kharif sowing in the region by 3.6 lakh hectares compared with the five-year average. More than 46 lakh hectares were eventually brought under kharif crops, but farmers have reported extensive damage after an almost dry Aug and Sept.While chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has announced “blanket” assistance for drought-affected farmers, the process of panchanamas is still in progress.
Article Summary: The district administration has removed three key administrative hurdles that were holding up crop credit. The move is aimed at ensuring that farmers who lost their kharif crops are not starved of working capital for the next season. The intervention comes amid widespread farm distress in Marathwada.

Article Title: Almost 100% crop loss seen, blanket compensation on the cards: Agriculture minister Bharne
Article Text:
Bharne with local MLA Babasaheb Deshmukh inspected crop damage in Sangola taluka of Solapur district

Kolhapur:





State agriculture minister Dattatray Bharne on Friday said crop loss assessment of over 1 crore hectares of kharif plantation has been completed and there is 100% loss in the drought-hit talukas. The compensation will thus not be partial but a blanket one, he added while speaking to the media after visiting fields in Sangola taluka of Solapur district.The minister said crop loss assessment has been completed on around 67% of total kharif plantations in the state. “In the next four days, the crop loss assessment of entire 1.49 cr hectares of area under kharif cultivation will be completed. There is no such thing as partial loss; there is 100% loss of the crops in drought hit talukas and therefore compensation will not be partial but a blanket one.”Bharne assured that the farmers will be compensated for crop loss before Diwali. “First, the compensation as per NDRF guidelines will be given to the farmers. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has assured maximum compensation as possible,” he said, stating that out of eight agricultural divisions, Amravati division is leading with 91% coverage of crop loss assessment, followed by Latur with 84%, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar with 70%, Pune with 58%, Nagpur with 48%, Nashik with 39%, Kolhapur with 29% and Konkan with 17%.The state has declared drought in 265 talukas and has now given directions to local authorities to carry out crop loss assessment in 18 additional talukas, as the local MLAs there have complained about severe water scarcity and crop damage.Bharne said that govt has released Rs 13,500 cr to waive the loans of the farmers with loan dues less than Rs 2 lakh; there are 30 lakh such farmers. “There are around 3 lakh farmers with loan amount more than Rs 2 lakh; the farmers will have to settle the amount over and above Rs 2 lakh. The third list of beneficiaries will be those who have paid the loans regularly; there are 22 lakh such farmers. Owing to some KYC issues and bank queries, the list got delayed, but soon, these farmers will also get the incentive promised as per Ahilyadevi Shetkari Karjmafi Yojana,” said Bharne.
Article Summary: State agriculture minister Dattatray Bharne on Friday said crop loss assessment of over 1 crore hectares of kharif plantation has been completed. The compensation will thus not be partial but a blanket one, he added while speaking to the media after visiting fields in Sangola taluka of Solapur district.
